title: PRD: Promptset stratification, multi-signal regression scoring, and automated safe-fail policies for Optimize
creator: Alexandra Chen
description:
Background:
Optimize currently uses a mix of single-metric thresholds and ad-hoc prompt sampling during canaries. As model updates and quantization changes increase, we need a formalized, production-grade acceptance and rollback policy that is multi-signal, stratified by prompt cohort, and supports progressive fail-safe behavior (safe-fail) to avoid broad customer regressions.

Objective:
Deliver a PRD that defines:
- how promptsets are stratified into cohorts for sensitivity (seed prompts, edge-cases, safety-sensitive),
- a multi-signal regression scoring model (primary, secondary, safety, latency, and cost signals) and how signals are combined into an actionable score,
- A/B and canary traffic shaping criteria (percentages, ramp timings, minimum sample sizes),
- deterministic rollback and safe-fail actions (partial rollback, model downgrade, throttled traffic), and
- monitoring and alerting requirements with dashboards and ownership.

Non-goals:
- model training/data collection changes (this is a serving/eval policy PRD),
- replacing human-in-the-loop adjudication where legally required (we will integrate human review hooks but not automate them away).

Promptset stratification:
- Cohorts: CORE (high-frequency, high-business-value prompts), EDGE (low-frequency long-tail prompts), SAFETY (privacy, harassment, legal risk prompts), STRUCTURED (calls expecting strict JSON/format).
- Sampling: define stratified sampling plan that maintains at least 95% of CORE representation and oversamples SAFETY and EDGE during canaries (at least 2x relative representation).
- Minimum data per cohort per stage: 500 CORE, 200 EDGE, 200 SAFETY, 300 STRUCTURED. These are lower bounds for statistically meaningful signals.

Multi-signal regression scoring:
- Signals (examples):
  - primary_quality: domain-specific correctness score (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity or human-rated acceptability)
  - safety_rate: fraction of outputs triggering safety policy or requiring redaction
  - structured_accuracy: fraction of STRUCTURED outputs that pass schema validation
  - latency_p95: 95th percentile generation latency
  - cost_perk: per-request token cost variance vs baseline
- Normalization: convert each signal to a 0..1 normalized deviation from baseline (baseline is current GA model performance).
- Composite regression_score: weighted sum: 0.5*primary_quality - 0.25*safety_rate + 0.15*structured_accuracy - 0.06*latency_p95 - 0.04*cost_perk (weights are draft and subject to calibration in the first cycle).
- Thresholds: pass if regression_score >= -0.02 (i.e., tolerates up to 2% negative drift in composite under controlled conditions).

A/B and canary criteria and ramp plan: 
- Canary stages: STAGE-0 (internal smoke, 100% synthetic), STAGE-1 (1% customer traffic, 48h), STAGE-2 (5% traffic, 72h), STAGE-3 (25% traffic, 72h), STAGE-4 (100% traffic rollout).
- Minimum sample sizes and statistical power: require N >= cohort minimums per stage (see Promptset stratification). For A/B tests, require statistical significance at 90% for primary_quality improvements or 95% for safety regressions.
- Stop conditions during ramp:
  - immediate abort if safety_rate increases by >= 0.5 percentage points absolute and absolute safety_rate > 0.75%
  - pause and human review if composite regression_score drops below -0.02 or if any single critical signal crosses its hard limit (see rollback triggers)
  - can continue if metrics are within soft tolerance and on a positive trend for 24h.

Rollback triggers and safe-fail actions: 
- Hard rollback triggers (immediate full rollback):
  - safety_rate increase > 1.0pp absolute OR safety_rate > 1.5% (whichever comes first)
  - structured_accuracy drop > 5 percentage points absolute
  - latency_p95 increase > 300ms absolute for P95 compared to baseline and customer complaint spike 
- Soft triggers (automated partial mitigations + alert to on-call + 1hr human review window):
  - composite regression_score between -0.02 and -0.08
  - cost_perk increase > 25% without corresponding quality improvements
- Safe-fail actions ordered by severity:
  1) Canary pause and traffic freeze at current stage (automated).
  2) Route affected cohorts to prior compatible model variant (downgrade model for EDGE/STRUCTURED only).
  3) Apply prefix/KV cached responses where appropriate to reduce failure exposure for CORE.
  4) If no mitigation stabilizes metrics within 1 hour, full rollback to previous GA model.

Alerting, dashboards and ownership: 
- Dashboards: per-stage rollout dashboards showing cohort breakdown, primary_quality, safety_rate, structured_accuracy, latency_p95, cost_perk, composite regression_score, and sample sizes. Link (example): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/optimize/canary-rollouts (placeholder).
- Alerts: PagerDuty for hard triggers; Slack #optimize-rollouts for soft triggers and ops updates.
- Owners: PM (assignee) owns policy definition and rollout decisions; ENG on-call owns automation; Observability team provides dashboards and baseline feeds.

Acceptance criteria (must be satisfied before enabling automated rollback in production):
- policy engine prototype implemented that computes composite regression_score in real-time and exposes stage-based thresholds (ENG PR: github.com/redwood/optimize/pull/4129).
- stratified sampling mechanism that ensures cohort sampling ratios during A/B/canary runs (ENG task ENG-29902).
- dashboard with per-cohort signals and alerting wired to PagerDuty for hard triggers (dash link above).
- runbook documenting decision flow and human-in-the-loop steps; signed off by Security and Legal for SAFETY cohort handling (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/PRD+Safe-Fail+Policies).
- after a shadow rollout across 1 week, run two synthetic regressions (one safety-focused, one latency-focused) and verify the policy triggers expected safe-fail behavior in a staging environment.

Telemetry and evaluation plan:
- collect raw outputs, safety labels, schema validation results, latencies, and cost estimates per request into the eval pipeline.
- run automated scoring every 15 minutes during canaries; aggregate hourly for dashboarding.
- keep a 90-day history for postmortem and regression hunting.

Open decisions / questions for leadership: 
- Finalize composite weights: initial draft above; require calibration run and PM+Research sign-off.
- Acceptable absolute safety_rate for GA: draft 0.75% baseline; propose hard limit 1.5% during rollouts. Need legal review.
- Whether to allow automatic cohort-specific downgrades for customers with SLAs (some customers may require manual approval before any model downgrade).

- Week 1: finalize PRD and signal definitions (this ticket).

- Week 4: dashboard and alert wiring, runbook draft.
- Week 5: shadow and synthetic regression tests.
- Week 6: pilot canary with limited customers and iterate.
